The monsoon surge that has brought strong to near gale winds to the 
Marianas over the last couple of days will persist tonight before 
beginning a weakening trend over the next couple of days. Although 
winds look to decrease towards the middle of the week, the monsoon 
looks to remain over the Marianas, keeping showers chances medium to 
high-end scattered (40-50%). The Wind Advisory remains in effect 
until 6 AM Wednesday. 20 to 30 mph winds with gusts to 40 mph will 
continue to be possible, especially in and around heavier showers. 
Winds look to decrease to 10 to 15 mph by Wednesday night as a short 
lull in higher winds moves over the region. 

Towards the latter half of the week, into this weekend, and into 
next week, the forecast is dependent on the location and strength of 
newly designated Invest 96W located south of Wake Island. Invest 96W 
is currently weak with an elongated circulation, see the tropical 
discussion for more details. The westerly winds feeding into Invest 
96W will intensify as the pressure gradient grows stronger. This 
will allow the monsoon to re-strengthen over the Marianas leading to 
a secondary surge. Uncertainty remains high on the placement of the 
monsoon surge. The GFS treats 96W more like a fully tropical system 
early next week, leading to stronger winds closer to the circulation 
and north of the CNMI. Meanwhile, the ECMWF has more of a 
subtropical appearance with the strong winds well south of the 
circulation, over the Marianas. The impacts would differ greatly 
with the potential for heavy rainfall and near gale winds near the 
center of the monsoon surge. A hydrological product may be needed in 
the coming days if confidence increases in the southern solution. 
Those in the Marianas should continue to monitor forecasts for 
updates in the progression of the monsoon.

Marine...
Fresh to strong westerlies with occasional gale force gusts 
will continue through early Wednesday morning across the Marianas, 
especially near heavier showers. The monsoon looks to briefly weaken 
over the next couple of days, before reinvigorating later this week. 
A distant swell from Typhoon Dolphin (12W) continues to make its way 
into the region and will begin to shift from the north to the 
northwest. Meanwhile, a strengthening west to southwest swell will 
continue to impact our region over the next week. This combination 
in swells and wind waves will keep seas around 10 feet across the 
coastal waters, maintaining hazardous sea conditions for much of the 
week. A Small Craft Advisory remains in effect through early Friday 
morning. 

A High Surf Advisory is in effect for west and north facing reefs, 
and a High Risk of Rip Currents is in effect for west, north, and 
east facing reefs of the Marianas. As monsoonal swells strengthen 
and period increases, surf could approach 12 feet across north 
facing reefs Wednesday night. A moderate risk of lightning is 
expected through the week. 

Tropical Systems...
A weak circulation, Joint Typhoon Warning Center's (JTWC) Invest 96W
is centered south-southeast of Wake Island near 16N164E. Invest 96W 
is currently rated sub-low, meaning development is possible, but not 
expected over the next few days. 96W is expected to slowly move WNW 
over the next few days, with model guidance showing little, if any, 
development as it progresses. Invest 96W will be monitored closely 
over the next few days, but it currently does not appear to be a 
threat to the Marianas or Micronesia.

Eastern Micronesia...
An abnormally dry regime has set up over eastern Micronesia, with
little to no convection expected over the next several days. Kosrae 
looks to be the driest point, with several days, including the
weekend, with POPs (Probability of Precipitation) less than 10 
percent to near zero. Pohnpei and Majuro don't look to fair much
better, with POPs remaining at or below 20 percent through the
weekend. 

For the marine forecast, expect gentle to moderate winds at Pohnpei
to become light to gentle Thursday and continue through the weekend.
For Kosrae and Majuro, light to gentle winds will prevail through the
weekend. Combined seas look to remain fairly stable through the
weekend as well.

Western Micronesia...
A monsoon pattern remains north of the region, shifting slightly 
north away from Yap this afternoon. A trailing line of showers 
remains stretched out across eastern Yap State, otherwise relatively 
quiet weather persists for much of the region this week. Then, a 
southern bend in the monsoon trough brings a return to scattered 
showers at Chuuk late week.

Combined seas have increased to 5 to 7 feet, with seas up to 8 feet

Palau, with moderate to fresh across Yap and Chuuk. As TY Dolphin
